rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> two-year field experiment (2014, 2015) in Beijing with 12 treatments in an RCB design, measuring deep percolation, NO3-N and E. coli. Q2: Results 'Nitrate leaching', Table 4 and Conclusion 2 <U+2013> cumulative NO3-N leaching at a given irrigation level generally increased as dripline (lateral) depth increased; in 2014 lateral depth had a significant effect (P=0.062), I1D3 being 189% and 86% higher than I1D1 and I1D2; sewage effluent irrigation gave higher leaching than groundwater (Table 5). Q4: Deep percolation section, Table 4 and Table 6 <U+2013> the study measured the intermediate variables (water flux at 70 cm from tensiometer pairs and NO3-N concentration in suction-cup leachate), showing deeper laterals gave greater deep percolation (I3D3 78% and 13% above I3D1) and higher leachate NO3-N concentration (23.2, 27.2, 36.2 mg/L for D1-D3 at I1 in 2015), attributed to a deeper wetted depth and NO3-N accumulation in deeper soil. Q7: Nitrate leaching section and Conclusions 1-2 <U+2013> from own data the authors state intensive rainfall (especially late season) was the driving force for NO3-N leaching and the mobile NO3-N content in soil the principal factor for the amount leached; the effect is stated to hold 'under our field conditions' in the semi-humid region. Q8: Nitrate leaching section <U+2013> authors note that the large seasonal precipitation compensated for treatment differences and that spatial variability of soil physical-chemical properties causes variability in leachate NO3-N and deep percolation, dampening the detectable influence of irrigation parameters; results are qualified as applying to their field conditions.
rows.notes: Q3: cumulative leaching is derived from a single approach (tensiometer-based Darcy flux times suction-cup concentration); soil NO3-N profile sampling is reported but not used as an independent estimate of leaching, so no triangulation. Q5/Q6: one site, one soil (silt loam), one crop (maize), plot scale. Q7 and Q8 are borderline: the rainfall/soil-N conditions and the spatial-variability caveat are stated by the authors but not framed formally as requirements/limitations. Q9: Table 6 gives SD and ranges only for leachate NO3-N concentrations; the cumulative seasonal NO3-N leaching values by lateral depth (Table 4) are single values (tensiometers in one replicate per treatment) with no dispersion measure, and significance is given only as P-values.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study tests subsurface drip irrigation with secondary sewage effluent (TSE) on maize in the North China Plain and directly reports the lateral-depth effect on seasonal NO3-N leaching cited in the passage.
